moments.label: Exceptional drought (D4) appears
moments.text: D4 first covers 1.2 % of the state in the week of 2020-12-15.
moments.src: US Drought Monitor county DSCI, California

moments.label: Peak extreme drought (D3+)
moments.text: D3 or worse reaches 89 % of California in the week of 2021-07-27 (county-weighted estimate).
moments.src: US Drought Monitor county DSCI, California

moments.label: Peak exceptional drought (D4)
moments.text: D4 reaches 49 % of California in the week of 2021-08-17 (county-weighted estimate; the official area-based figure was about 46 % on 14 Sep 2021).
moments.src: US Drought Monitor county DSCI, California

moments.label: Lake Oroville low
moments.text: Lake Oroville stored 0.79 million acre-feet in the week of 2021-09-21, its lowest in the replay.

moments.label: Shasta Lake low
moments.text: Shasta Lake stored 0.97 million acre-feet in the week of 2021-10-19, its lowest in the replay.

moments.label: Peak severe drought (D2+)
moments.text: D2 or worse reaches 98 % of California in the week of 2022-05-24 (county-weighted estimate).
moments.src: US Drought Monitor county DSCI, California

moments.label: End of the replay
moments.text: By 2023-12-26, D2 or worse covers 0 % of the state.
moments.src: US Drought Monitor county DSCI, California

teaches.title: One wet winter does not end a drought
teaches.text: Reservoirs and soil recover after wet months, but Central Valley wells and groundwater lag. Switch on the wells and the groundwater layer to see what the map alone hides.
